name: PetaSats
description: Buys BSV with USDC on Base from an AI app through a local MCP server. The kit's keys stay on this device and each swap settles as a cross-chain atomic swap with the PetaSats market maker. Quote and status tools keep your existing policy; the swap and the two withdrawal tools move funds and need review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Keep swap_asset_to_bsv, withdraw_bsv and withdraw_base on review: each one moves funds. get_quote, fund_wallet and list_liquidity are read-only and move nothing.
Create ~/.petasats/limits.json: bsvDestinations and baseDestinations allowlist where funds may go, and maxSwapUsdPerDay caps daily swaps. The kit rereads it before every money operation.
Keep shell and file-write access to ~/.petasats on review: an agent that can edit limits.json or the STOP file can undo those limits.
Use stop_spending to stop new swaps and withdrawals at once. Only the user can resume, from a terminal (npx petasats-mcp@0.2.15 resume); recovery of swaps already started keeps working.
Leave speed at standard, the default, which waits for one BSV confirmation, or set allowFastSettlement to false. Fast settlement accepts an unconfirmed BSV lock and is limited to $25.
Never let an agent read, print or send ~/.petasats/keys.json; it holds the only copy of the kit's keys, so keep a private backup.
This listing launches the reviewed release, petasats-mcp@0.2.15. Keep a pinned version in your own configuration too, so only a reviewed release runs.
